findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tie the deferred live Anthropic+Bedrock canary (AC-6) to a NAMED tracking child/ticket that must complete before the cutover is considered fully closed, so the defaulted live provider path is not validated solely by offline oracle + static census.
evidence: '[operator-attested] Direct Anthropic and Bedrock canaries pass with secrets absent... DEFERRED to a credentialed human operator (see tracking comment).'
'the retry-layer/cache-accounting contract is pinned offline by the AC-1/3/4 oracle + documented (AC-8)'

E5: proxy-validation of a defaulted/cutover path is MAJOR unless the live exercise is 'explicitly deferred to a NAMED child ticket' — here it is deferred to a tracking comment / unnamed operator, not a named child.
findings.finding: This is a cutover that makes the one-operation Pydantic path the DEFAULT structured-output path for every consumer, yet the ONLY end-to-end/live validation of the defaulted provider boundary (Anthropic + Bedrock cache read/write/input counts and complete-vs-omit wire observations) is deferred (AC-6 is unchecked, operator-attested) to a 'credentialed human operator (see tracking comment)' — not a named child ticket. The offline AC-1/3/4 oracle and AST census exercise the path only through mocks/static analysis, so the plan can close green while the live provider path (cache accounting, actual same-run retry over the wire) is never exercised as it will run in production.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC-6 (operator-attested) and Testing 'direct Anthropic and Bedrock same-run retry canaries'
scenarios: The cutover closes as done with every offline AC green, but the live Anthropic/Bedrock cache accounting or same-run ModelRetry path regresses (e.g. request-budget addend trips before the output-retry counter under real transport) and no test in this plan would have caught it — the break surfaces only in production for a library/CLI/MCP consumer hitting a real provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'see tracking comment' with a concrete named follow-up ticket id that owns the credentialed live canary, and state that the cutover's live-path acceptance remains open until that named ticket records the cache read/write/input counts and complete/omit branch.
